seoTitle: Online Pomodoro Timer - Boost Your Productivity
metaDescription: A free online Pomodoro Timer to help you focus. Work in 25-minute intervals, take regular breaks, and maximize your daily productivity.
intro: Struggling to stay focused and productive? The Pomodoro Technique is one of the most scientifically backed time management methods available, and our free online Pomodoro Timer makes it effortless to practice. The core idea is simple: work in focused 25-minute intervals (called Pomodoros) separated by short 5-minute breaks, with a longer 15–30 minute break after every four Pomodoros. This rhythm prevents burnout, reduces mental fatigue, and dramatically increases your ability to concentrate on demanding tasks. Our timer handles the entire cycle automatically, so all you need to do is press Start and focus on your work.
whatIs: A Pomodoro Timer is a specialized countdown timer designed around the Pomodoro Technique, a time management method invented by Francesco Cirillo in the late 1980s. The technique uses a simple alternating pattern of focused work sessions and rest breaks to maintain peak mental performance throughout the day. Our implementation provides configurable work and break durations, automatic cycling between work and break phases, session counting to track your daily progress, and audio notifications to signal transitions. It is an all-in-one productivity tool that runs entirely in your browser—no installation, no account, and no data collection.
howToUse: Select your mode: 'Pomodoro' for working, 'Short Break' for quick rests, or 'Long Break' for extended recovery.
Click the 'Start' button to begin the timer.
Work completely focused on a single task until the timer reaches zero.
When the timer ends, take a break. The tool tracks your completed Pomodoros automatically.
howItWorks: The timer operates on a repeating cycle: a 25-minute work phase followed by a 5-minute short break, repeated four times, after which a longer 15-minute break occurs. When you press Start, the timer begins counting down the work phase. At zero, an audio notification alerts you that it is time for a break, and the timer automatically switches to the break countdown. After the break ends, another notification signals that the next work phase is starting. The session counter increments after each completed work phase, giving you a clear visual record of how many Pomodoros you have completed. All durations are configurable if you prefer different interval lengths.
workedExample: Imagine you have a research paper to write. You press Start on the Pomodoro Timer and begin your first 25-minute work session. The timer counts down from 25:00. When it hits 00:00, an alert sounds and the display switches to a 5-minute break. You stand up, stretch, and get water. When the break ends, another alert signals the start of your second 25-minute session. After four complete work sessions (totaling 100 minutes of focused work), the timer switches to a long 15-minute break. By the end of this cycle, you have completed 4 Pomodoros and logged nearly 2 hours of deep, focused writing.
resultInterpretation: The timer display shows the remaining time in the current phase (either work or break). A visual indicator or label tells you which phase you are in—Work, Short Break, or Long Break. The session counter shows how many Pomodoros (work sessions) you have completed so far. Tracking your daily Pomodoro count helps you understand your productive capacity—most people find that 8–12 Pomodoros represent a full day of truly focused work. If you consistently achieve fewer, it may indicate too many interruptions; if more, you might be working without adequate rest, which can lead to diminishing returns.
useCases: Studying: Breaking dense study material into manageable chunks for better retention.
Programming: Focusing deeply on writing code or solving a bug without checking emails.
Writing: Overcoming writer's block by committing to write for just 25 minutes.
tipsAndLimitations: Keep the browser tab open and active to ensure the timer runs perfectly.
If you get distracted during a Pomodoro, the strict rule is to either stop the timer entirely or power through—no pausing allowed in the original method, though our tool allows it for convenience.

faq.question: Can I change the duration of the Pomodoro?
faq.answer: Currently, the tool uses the scientifically backed standard times (25 min work, 5 min short break, 15 min long break) to guarantee maximum effectiveness.

faq.question: What is the Pomodoro Technique?
faq.answer: It is a time management method developed by Francesco Cirillo in the late 1980s. It uses a timer to break work into intervals, separated by breaks.

cta: Start your first Pomodoro and crush your tasks!
disclaimer: This tool is for personal productivity tracking. It relies on your browser's timing functions.
